details: Tensorlake@0.5.144 adds a preinstall hook (`node lib/setup.mjs`) that executes a self-propagating credential- and wallet-stealing npm worm. The hook loads lib/Math_Symbol.js (856 KB of javascript-obfuscator output — a large encoded string array plus a custom base64/XOR decoder) which sets the marker `globalThis.WORMTAG='tensrlake'` and then: 1. Token theft and self-propagation — reads the npm publish token from `.npmrc`/`~/.npmrc`, validates it against `hxxps://registry[.]npmjs[.]org/-/whoami`, confirms the token has write scope, enumerates every package owned by that maintainer via `hxxps://registry[.]npmjs[.]org/-/v1/search?text=maintainer:<user>&size=250`, and re-publishes the same payload into those packages. 2. Secret and wallet harvesting — walks a hardcoded path table covering `~/.ssh/id_rsa`, `~/.ssh/id_dsa`, `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`, `~/.aws`, `~/.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json`, `~/.vault-token`, `/root/.kube/config`, `.git-credentials`, `~/.terraform.d/credentials.tfrc.json`, `~/.config/solana/id.json`, `~/.electrum/wallets/*`, `~/.electrum-ltc/wallets/*`, `~/.zcash/wallet.dat`, `~/.config/Exodus/exodus.wallet/*`, `~/Library/Application Support/MetaMask/*`, `~/.foundry/keystores/*`, `~/.keplr/*`, `~/.ledger/config.json`, `~/.config/sui/sui_config/sui.keystore`, `~/.cosmos/config/priv_validator_key.json`, `~/.config/1Password/1password.sqlite`, Firefox `key4.db`, Chromium/Vivaldi extension IndexedDB stores, and AI-assistant configs (`~/.cursor/cli-config.json`, `~/.codex/config.toml`, `~/.gemini/config.json`, `~/.codeium/config.json`, `~/.continue/config.json`). 3. Persistence — writes `.vscode/tasks.json`, `.vscode/setup.mjs`, `.claude/settings.json` and `.claude/setup.mjs` into the working tree and drops `setup.mjs` at `process.cwd()/dist/setup.mjs`, so the payload re-executes when the project is opened in an editor or agent tool. 4. Second stage — resolves a platform key from `process.platform`/`process.arch`, builds a download URL from the repository path, fetches a platform-specific binary with `https`, executes it via `execFileSync`, then deletes the temporary directory. The hook deliberately no-ops when `CI`, `GITHUB_ACTIONS`, `GITLAB_CI` or `RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT` is set, keeping it dormant in automated build environments. The package's own SDK code is otherwise intact; the worm is injected into the published tarball. tensorlake@0.5.144 ships an obfuscated preinstall hook (`node lib/setup.mjs`) that downloads a platform-specific native binary, extracts it and executes it, and deliberately no-ops when CI, GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITLAB_CI or RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT is set so it only fires on developer machines. The hook loads lib/Math_Symbol.js, an 856 KB obfuscated bundle that sets `globalThis.WORMTAG='tensrlake'` and harvests developer credentials and wallets: ~/.ssh/id_rsa, ~/.ssh/id_dsa, ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, ~/.npmrc,.git-credentials, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.config/gcloud/application_default_credentials.json, ~/.vault-token, ~/.terraform.d/credentials.tfrc.json, ~/.config/1Password/1password.sqlite, MetaMask/Exodus/Electrum/Zcash/Sui/Cosmos/Keplr wallet files, Firefox key4.db and Chrome/Vivaldi IndexedDB stores, and AI CLI configs (~/.cursor/cli-config.json, ~/.codex/config.toml, ~/.gemini/config.json, %USERPROFILE%\.cursor\mcp.json). It then reads the npm auth token, enumerates every package the victim can write via the npm registry API (hxxps://registry[.]npmjs[.]org/-/v1/search?text=maintainer:<user>&size=250 and the org/team package endpoints), downloads those tarballs and republishes them carrying the same payload. In GitHub Actions it also takes the OIDC identity token from the environment and exchanges it for a Fulcio signing certificate (/api/v1/signingCert) so the republished packages carry valid provenance. Worm tag: tensrlake. The malicious lib/ directory is not part of the upstream SDK source tree. The published tarball of this SDK carries an injected preinstall hook (`node lib/setup.mjs`) that loads an obfuscated 856 KB payload, `lib/Math_Symbol.js`. The payload sets a global marker (`globalThis.WORMTAG='tensrlake'`) and then harvests credentials from the installing machine: `~/.npmrc` and `.npmrc`, `~/.aws/credentials`, `~/.ssh/id_rsa` and `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`, `~/.git-credentials`, `~/.vault-token`, `~/.terraform.d/credentials.tfrc.json`, `~/.config/gcloud/credentials.db` and `application_default_credentials.json`, `/root/.kube/config`, `~/.config/solana/id.json`, `~/.foundry/keystores/*`, `~/.cosmos/config/priv_validator_key.json`, `~/.config/sui/sui_config/sui.keystore`, `~/.keplr/*`, `~/.electrum*/wallets/*`, `~/.config/Exodus/exodus.wallet/*`, `~/Library/Application Support/MetaMask/*`, `~/.ledger/config.json`, `~/.config/1Password/1password.sqlite`, `~/.local/share/keyrings/login.keyring`, Firefox `key4.db`, and a long list of AI/CI CLI config files (`~/.codex/config.toml`, `~/.gemini/config.json`, `~/.cursor/cli-config.json`, `~/.codeium/config.json`, `~/.continue/config.json`, `~/.circleci/cli.yml`, `~/.config/hardhat/config.json`). It also reads CI environment variables (GITHUB_TOKEN, GITHUB_WORKFLOW_REF, GITHUB_REPOSITORY, GITLAB_CI, CI, VAULT_TOKEN, VAULT_AUTH_TOKEN), uses the stolen npm token to enumerate the victim's published packages and scopes with write access, and uses the stolen GitHub token against api[.]github[.]com to fetch repository contents and commit/push files into the victim's own repositories — worm-style self-propagation. It writes `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` for persistence and fingerprints the host (hostname, username, OS, cwd, locale). The hook deliberately returns early when CI, GITHUB_ACTIONS or GITLAB_CI is set, so it stays dormant inside build pipelines and only executes on developer workstations. Transport endpoints observed: api[.]github[.]com and registry[.]npmjs[.]org, abused as the exfiltration and propagation channel; no attacker-owned C2 domain is present. tensorlake@0.5.144 ships a preinstall hook ("node lib/setup.mjs") that loads an obfuscated 856 KB payload, lib/Math_Symbol.js, which executes automatically on npm install. The payload sets a global marker (globalThis.WORMTAG='tensrlake') and harvests credentials and developer secrets from the installing machine: ~/.ssh/authorized_keys and SSH private keys, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.npmrc, ~/.git-credentials, ~/.docker/config.json, ~/.vault-token, ~/.config/gcloud/*, ~/.terraform.d/credentials.tfrc.json, ~/.config/1Password/1password.sqlite, browser profile key4.db, cryptocurrency wallets (~/.electrum/wallets/*, ~/.config/Exodus/exodus.wallet/*, ~/.zcash/wallet.dat, ~/.keplr/*, ~/.cosmos/config/priv_validator_key.json, ~/.config/sui/sui_config/sui.keystore) and AI-assistant/IDE configs (~/.claude/settings.json, ~/.codex/config.toml, ~/.gemini/config.json, ~/.cursor/cli-config.json). It reads CI/CD secrets (GITHUB_TOKEN, GITHUB_WORKFLOW_REF, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, VAULT_TOKEN), then uses a stolen npm token to enumerate every package the victim can publish and re-injects itself into those packages as.claude/setup.mjs /.vscode/setup.mjs with a preinstall hook, republishing them — self-propagating worm behaviour. It beacons host/user/OS metadata in an AES-GCM-encrypted envelope over HTTPS to a remote endpoint (port 443, /hbd/ path) and executes the JavaScript returned by that server via eval(), giving the operator remote code execution on the installer's machine; it also downloads a second-stage binary from the same host's /hbd/ path and writes it to a temporary file. The payload skips execution when CI/GITHUB_ACTIONS/GITLAB_CI is set and exits the process after dispatching. The C2 hostname is stored obfuscated in the bundle; the port (443) and the /hbd/ URL path are the observable network indicators.
